I fetched sources it (Wayback copy of the sil.org PDF; live site returns a Cloudflare 403), scanned it, and read the stress passages on the page images: p.2 'Stress is... generally predictable. Penultimate stress is found in the great majority of the words'; sec. 5.3.1 p.23 'Stress and tone are not considered to be phonemic at the word level. sources.citation: Conrad, Bob, Joshua Lukas & John Alungum. 1977. Preliminary Phonology of Mufian (Southern Arapesh). Manuscript, SIL, Ukarumpa. 37 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 51990; posted 2009 'as is'). fetched sources via Wayback id_ copy of sil.org reapdata PDF (live URL Cloudflare-403); image-only PDF, scanned (tesseract, 200 dpi) to.
sources.quote: p.2: 'Stress is not usually written, since it is generally predictable. Penultimate stress is found in the great majority of the words. When it is necessary to write stress, a ' is placed before the stressed syllable.' p.23: 'Stress and tone are not considered to be phonemic at the word level. In isolation, the majority of words have penultimate stress, and high tone usually occurs on the stressed syllable.' (examples p.23-24 all penultimate: 'isag, a'liga, wam'bele?w, ona'howa, kopisia'howa, alupu'tina). p.27: 'Stress placement on the vowels of a complex nucleus is usually distributed about e
sources.locator: Introduction, printed p.2 (PDF p.3); sec. 5.3.1 'Phonemic status of tone, stress, length', printed pp.23-24 (PDF pp.24-25); sec. 7.1, printed pp.26-27 (PDF pp.27-28)
sources.note: The primary phonology write-up behind the 4-page 1992 OPD our coding quotes; has a dedicated suprasegmentals section (5.3.1) with stress-marked examples and a phonological-word definition ('one and only one stress'). fetched sources now; confirms penultimate, non-phonemic stress.
